rows.description: An adult notices that a partner not sharing every message or feeling is not automatically cheating. Trust means allowing a private inner life, while still expecting honesty about things that affect the relationship.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A teenager who prides themselves on being brutally honest tells a friend her singing is bad and calls it truth. Bluntness can serve the speaker's need to feel superior more than the listener's growth.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult learns that the same true feedback can be said with care, at the right moment, or as a weapon. Honesty joined with kindness is harder than either alone and lasts longer.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Receiving hard truth from someone who cares [Receiver]
rows.description: An adult hears a difficult truth about their work or habit from a friend and first feels stung, then grateful. Truth from someone invested in you usually shows in the effort taken to say it gently.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler with crumbs on the face says no biscuit. It is a hopeful reflex, not cunning, and the child cannot yet model what the adult already knows.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12

rows.description: A preschooler learns the adult cannot see their mind, and tries a lie to avoid trouble or gain a treat. This shows growing theory of mind and is a developmental step, not moral failure.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12

rows.description: A parent says telling the truth matters more than the mistake, and responds to a confession with calm repair and thanks. Asking traps such as who did this is avoided, since they invite lying.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12
related mind states: gratitude, calm, trust

rows.description: A parent sees a child claim an invisible friend or a made-up adventure. Pretend and wish stories are normal play, and calling them lies shames a healthy imagination.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6

rows.description: A child who is beaten or humiliated for confessing learns that lying is safer than truth. Fear of punishment is the strongest teacher of deception.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6
related mind states: fear, humiliation, trust

rows.description: Children watch adults tell white lies on the phone, or brag, or cheat on small rules. Adults who own their own errors openly teach more about honesty than any lecture does.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6
